svg.title: Hawking radiation from a black hole
svg.desc: A rough picture of Hawking radiation. Particle–antiparticle pairs appear just outside a black hole’s event horizon. Sometimes one member falls in while the other escapes: an electron escapes while its positron falls in, and a proton escapes while its antiproton falls in. Sometimes both fall in, as for a muon pair. Sometimes both escape, and an escaping electron and positron annihilate into gamma rays that escape. The escaping radiation carries away energy, reducing the black hole’s mass.
